summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, kidney transplantation, and breast cancer was admitted for acute onset of nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, and myalgias after eating a chicken-Asian salad. Initial evaluation showed no bacterial source, with negative urinalysis, negative flu swab, and normal chest X-ray. Blood and urine cultures were obtained, with urine showing gram-positive bacteria but no definitive pathogen. CMV viral load was negative. She was managed supportively with IV fluids and symptom control. Her symptoms improved over 3 days, and she was discharged home on her baseline immunosuppressive and diabetes medications with a prescription for ondansetron for breakthrough nausea. The clinical course was consistent with viral gastroenteritis.
